headline: The UK government has accepted all 44 recommendations of a commission led by NHS doctors on AI in healthcare, and says AI medical devices will need continual monitoring after approval.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: an official UK policy decision confirmed by the government and Reuters, though the detailed rules are still to come.
importance_line: Patients treated with AI-based medical devices in the UK would see them watched after approval rather than checked once, and hospitals and developers would work under continuing oversight, but the detailed rules are still to be written.
summary: Reuters reports that the UK government has accepted all 44 recommendations of a commission on regulating AI in healthcare, and that Lawrence Tallon, head of the medicines regulator, the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), says AI-based medical devices will need constant monitoring after approval, not one safety check beforehand. The government adds that the commission, an independent panel led by NHS doctors that reported on 10 Sep 2026, concluded that such devices should be assessed throughout their working life, not just once, and promises draft guidance by December 2026 and a full plan by spring 2027.
